title: fix(app-shell): store only the patch in a view personalization overlay (#5233)
body:
Fixes #5233

The write half of the maintainer's 2026-08-12 ruling (objectstack#7494, comment
`5261754173`), unblocked by objectstack#9933 landing in `@objectstack/spec` 17.1.0.
The read half (`narrowPersonalizationOverlay`) merged earlier as PR #5272 and stays.

## Premise check first — this card's own history says it is step one

The 2026-08-18 dispatch measured the ruling's premise **false** and escalated instead
of proceeding: `ViewMetadataSchema` refused a `columnState`-only patch, so writing the
patch alone would have made a column drag 422 rather than persist. The unlock sweep was
explicit that admitting `columnState` as a runtime-only overlay key and making it
*author-writable* are two different spec changes, and only the first shipped — so the
first thing measured here was **which one the pin gives us**.

Probed against the installed `@objectstack/spec` **17.1.0** (resolved from
`packages/app-shell`, version read off the resolved `package.json`, not the lockfile):

| probe | reading |
|:--|:--|
| `{ object, name, viewKind, columnState }` | **ACCEPT** |
| `{ … sort }` / `{ … rowHeight }` / `{ … hiddenFields }` / `{ … inlineEdit }` alone | **ACCEPT** |
| `columnStates` (typo neighbour) | REFUSE — "Not a `view` body: no recognized `view` key" |
| `columnstate` (typo neighbour) | REFUSE — same |
| `zzzNotAKey` | REFUSE — same |
| `columnState: { widths: { a: 'wide' } }` | REFUSE — the inner shape is genuinely validated, not `.strip()`ed |
| `columnState` with no `object` / no `viewKind` | REFUSE — identity is required on the overlay face |
| an **authored** `ViewItem` carrying `columnState` | REFUSE |

The refusals are the control the accepts need: the same probe still says no, so the
five accepts are a reading and not a schema that stopped discriminating. The admission
is the **runtime-only** one the ruling asked for, not authorability — the spec's own
text says so: `columnState` is declared on `flattenedViewOverlayFields()` (the overlay
validation face) and `viewItemWireFields()`, and the authoring door carries a rejection
message for it by name ("Column order/widths are per-user runtime personalization …
Remove it from authored metadata"). **Premise holds. Proceeding was correct.**

*Instrument limits:* this probes the schema `saveMetaItem` validates against, in-process.
It does not exercise a live server, so it cannot speak to identity inheritance actually
running server-side — that is why the write still sends `viewKind` when the active tab
has one, rather than relying on inheritance.

## Landing site — the triage line is inverted, re-measured on `9850c6e4e`

Triage says the fix lands in `packages/data-objectstack`. It does not:

- `persistViewPatch` is **defined** at `packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx:738`.
- The fat write was at **`ObjectView.tsx:766-771`** —
  `dataSource.updateViewConfig(objectName, viewIdLocal, { ...baseViewDef, ...merged }, { isSavedView: targetIsSavedView })`.
- `packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts:1337-1345` holds a docblock that **describes**
  the defect. The adapter is not the defect; it persists what it is given, and that is
  correct. Only that docblock changed there — no adapter behaviour.

## What "store only the patch" means here — and where it deliberately stops

`merged` is the debounced accumulation of the third argument of every `persistViewPatch`
call. All **seven** call sites pass a single-key object literal, one owned key each
(`rowHeight`, `sort`, `hiddenFields`, `columnState`, `inlineEdit`) — so `merged` **is**
the patch, and it is written verbatim rather than filtered through
`VIEW_OVERLAY_OWNED_KEYS`: a filter here would silently drop a sixth key someone later
persists, which is the drift the existing `PERSIST_CALLS` ratchet exists to make loud.

The line between *owned* and *copied* is not redrawn here — it was drawn on the read
side by PR #5272 and this write now produces exactly the shape that reader keeps:
owned keys plus `VIEW_OVERLAY_IDENTITY_KEYS`. `object`, `name` and the overlay marker
are stamped by `updateViewConfig` itself; `viewKind` is carried from the active tab when
it has one (identity, not content) and omitted otherwise. `label` is **not** kept — the
platform inherits it from the shadowed registry entry, so a stored one is a snapshot of
the source view's label at write time, which is the class of frozen key the whole card
is about. The ruling's own examples of the frozen copy — `filter`, `columns`, `label`,
`type`, `isDefault` — are all gone.

### The branch, and why narrowing both sides would be the worse error

**`updateViewConfig` persists through `client.meta.saveItem`, which is a `PUT` of the
whole document.** The adapter's own `updateView` reads the current row and merges onto
it *precisely because* `saveItem` does not — its 404 path says so in as many words
("there is nothing to merge onto. Fail loudly instead of emitting the partial write").
So the body handed to `updateViewConfig` is what the row **becomes**.

- **system view (`isSavedView: false`)** — the row is an overlay laid over a definition
  that lives elsewhere. Nothing in it but the patch is an opinion the user expressed.
  **Narrowed.** This is the card.
- **saved view (`isSavedView: true`)** — the row **is** the view. There is no source
  underneath it for a copied key to shadow, so the ruled harm cannot arise; a patch-only
  PUT would not narrow this row, it would **delete the user's view definition**. Left
  byte-identical to the pre-fix write.

That is not an argument, it is measured — see ablation C below, which quotes the
destroyed `config`. Considered and rejected: routing the saved-view branch through
`updateView` (read-modify-write) would narrow it honestly, but it changes which adapter
method the toolbar uses, doubles the requests, throws where the current path upserts,
and is outside both this ruling and this fence.

### Existing rows: both dispositions, neither silent

Tolerate on read (PR #5272) still holds — and because this write replaces the whole
document, **the next toolbar toggle also strips a pre-fix fat row at rest**. So the
issue's "strip on next write" arrives as a consequence rather than as a second
mechanism. No migration. Both are pinned.

## The demonstration

Same scenario twice through the **real** adapter write, the **real** batch read and the
**real** consumer merge — a user drags a column on `crm_lead.default`, then an admin
edits that view's filter from `status=open` to `status=qualified`:

```
──────── PRE-FIX WRITE   { ...baseViewDef, ...patch } ────────
  sys_metadata row keys                    : _isOverride, columnState, columns, filter, isDefault, label, name, object, type
  row.filter AT REST                       : [{"field":"status","operator":"equals","value":"open"}]
  tab.filter the user's list queries with   : [{"field":"status","operator":"equals","value":"qualified"}]
  RAW merge (a reader with no read-side narrowing):
    effective filter                       : [{"field":"status","operator":"equals","value":"open"}]      ← the admin's edit does NOT arrive
    effective label                        : "All Leads"
    effective columns                      : ["name","status"]

──────── POST-FIX WRITE  buildPersistedViewBody(...) ────────
  sys_metadata row keys                    : _isOverride, columnState, name, object, viewKind
  row.filter AT REST                       : undefined
  tab.filter the user's list queries with   : [{"field":"status","operator":"equals","value":"qualified"}]
  RAW merge (a reader with no read-side narrowing):
    effective filter                       : [{"field":"status","operator":"equals","value":"qualified"}]  ← it arrives
    effective label                        : "All Leads (active)"
    effective columns                      : ["name","status","owner"]
```

Read this honestly: **through objectui's own switcher the two rows already behave the
same** — that is PR #5272 doing exactly the job it was merged for. What this PR changes
is the bytes at rest and, with them, every reader that does **not** run
`narrowPersonalizationOverlay`: Studio and the server-side switcher merge the stored
document over the source view with no such pass, and for them the frozen copy still won.
That is the half the maintainer called a transition rather than an end state, and the
"laundering an unrecognized key past validation" the ruling names.

Both legs are pinned as tests, not just printed: `a reader OUTSIDE objectui — no
read-side narrowing — now sees the admin edit too` runs the pre-fix row first as its own
control, so the post-fix assertions are a measurement rather than a tautology.

## The existing guard, moved deliberately

`ObjectView.overlayPatchOnly.test.ts` pinned the **current** fat-write shape. What moved,
and what did not:

- **Moved (comment only, assertions untouched):** the first case's fixture was documented
  as "EXACTLY what `persistViewPatch` sends". It now says **USED TO send**, and the case
  is retitled `a PRE-FIX fat overlay no longer shadows the source view on read`. The body
  is still produced by the **real** adapter write rather than dropped into the store, so
  it models a row a real write path once produced. Its assertions are unchanged and still
  pass — the read-side half is not weakened by an inch.
- **Not moved:** the `PERSIST_CALLS` ratchet over every `persistViewPatch(…)` call site.
  The fix is inside the callee, so all seven call sites are byte-identical and the ratchet
  reads exactly as before.
- **Added:** a second ratchet — the `updateViewConfig` call site must route its body
  through `buildPersistedViewBody(` and must not contain `...baseViewDef`. Ablation B
  below is why: without it, reverting the wiring alone leaves **every** behavioural test
  green.

Sibling assumptions checked, as the dispatch asked:
`ObjectView.overlayFilterRecovery.test.tsx:150` and
`ObjectView.defaultViewIdentity.test.tsx:238` — neither becomes false.
`defaultViewIdentity`'s docblock is about the persistence *key* (`name: viewId`), which
is unchanged, so it is left alone. `overlayFilterRecovery`'s comment claimed the copy in
the present tense and is tense-corrected; its legacy-triple case still routes past the
narrowing (no marker, no `viewKind`) and still passes.

## Reverse verification — three ablations, predictions recorded before running

Each: commit first, mutate, confirm on disk by **anchored counts in both directions**
(the deleted anchor and an injected `ABLATION_x` marker), run, restore under
`trap … EXIT INT TERM`, then confirm the restore in both directions too. No rebuild is
involved or possible to get wrong here: the root `vitest.config.mts` aliases
`@object-ui/data-objectstack` to `packages/data-objectstack/src`, and `ObjectView.tsx`
is imported from source — the ablations turning red *is* the proof of that resolution.

| leg | mutation | predicted | observed |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **A** | the seam's overlay branch reverted to `{ ...baseViewDef, ...patch }` | 6 red / 11 green — the six write assertions; the saved-view guard and the wiring ratchet **survive** | **exactly that** |
| **B** | seam kept, the *wiring* reverted at the call site | **1 red** — the wiring ratchet **only**; all 16 others green | **exactly that** |
| **C** | narrow **both** branches (the over-strict reading) | 2 red — both saved-view guards | **exactly that**, failing with `expected undefined to deeply equal { type: 'kanban', …(1) }` |

Leg B is the one worth reading twice: it is the gap a behavioural-only test suite cannot
see, and the reason the second ratchet exists. Leg C is the control that must **survive**
legs A and B and must **die** here — it is what says the narrowing stopped where it
should, and its failure text is the user's deleted view.

## Verification

At `9a5fce746` (the final commit; the union below was run on this tree).

| check | reading |
|:--|:--|
| dependency closure | `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...' build` → exit 0 |
| `vitest run packages/app-shell/ packages/data-objectstack/` | `Test Files 543 passed (543)` · `Tests 5475 passed \| 1 skipped (5476)` |
| re-run after the comment pass | `Test Files 342 passed (342)` · `Tests 3496 passed \| 1 skipped (3497)`, 0 failures |
| the guard file | `Test Files 1 passed (1)` · `Tests 17 passed (17)` |
| `type-check` (both packages) | both script names echoed — `packages/data-objectstack type-check$ tsc --noEmit … Done`, `packages/app-shell type-check$ tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json … Done` — so neither was a zero-match silent pass |
| `check:control-bytes` | `✅ check-control-bytes: OK (scanned 4803 tracked text file(s); skipped 85 binary)` |
| `check:phantom-deps` | `✅ Every in-scope import is declared by the package that publishes it.` |
| `check:self-import` | `✅ No package names itself inside its own src/.` |
| `check:esm-specifiers` | `Specifier leg: no un-ledgered package emits an extensionless relative specifier.` |
| `check:spec-symbols` | `✅ spec symbol derivation: 1298 files scanned against 4966 spec export names` |
| `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` | ✅ No changeset declares a **major** bump. |
| `check-changeset-presence.mjs` | `✅ 9 source file(s) of 2 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)` |
| `check-lint-coverage.mjs` | `✅ lint coverage: 46/46 packages linted, 0 with outstanding errors (0 total)` |
| control bytes over the diff | 0 hits, **controlled**: the same instrument over the same 10 files finds 47 `persistViewPatch` hits |

**Lint was narrowed, and the narrowing is declared with its evidence.** `pnpm lint` is
`turbo run lint`, i.e. each package's own `eslint .`. Run for the two packages that
contain changed files: **935 files / 0 errors / 2560 warnings** (app-shell) and **48 files
/ 0 errors / 368 warnings** (data-objectstack), plus `lint:root` → 0 errors. (1) The
population is eslint's own — `eslint .` under each package resolving the root
`eslint.config.js` and its ignores, not a file list I chose; (2) the counts are read off
`--format json`; (3) the narrowing excludes nothing, because type-aware linting is **not
enabled** — the config extends `tseslint.configs.recommended`, not `recommendedTypeChecked`,
and `languageOptions` declares no `project`/`projectService`, so no file outside those two
packages can have its verdict moved by this diff. Warnings are pre-existing
`no-explicit-any` in an `any`-typed file; eslint exits 0 (no `--max-warnings` anywhere),
and `+2` of them are the new seam's own loosely-typed record signature, matching the
surrounding file.

`Build Docs` is red on `main` (#5668) and this diff touches neither `apps/site/` nor
`content/`, so a ~10-second skip there is expected and is **not** a reading that the docs
site builds.

## Fence

Written: `packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx` · four
`packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.*.test.*` · `packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts`
(**the `:1337-1345` docblock only**) · four `packages/data-objectstack/src/*.test.ts`
(comment tense only) · `.changeset/*`. Nothing under `apps/console/.env.*`,
`examples/console-starter/**` or `packages/auth/**`. `narrowPersonalizationOverlay`'s own
docblock was left alone on purpose: its "strip-on-next-write heals a row only when its
user touches that view again" is still a true statement about that disposition, and it is
outside the granted docblock.
